phases.title: Computation and the Machine
phases.topics: computation; information representation; binary and number systems; Boolean logic; gates; digital circuits; CPU; memory; machine language; assembly; hardware/software boundary
phases.outcome: Trace a small instruction through a designed machine; predict state changes before simulation.

phases.title: Programming
phases.topics: fundamentals; C; Python; data types; functions; recursion; data structures; pointers; memory management; files; debugging; testing; Git
phases.outcome: Implement and debug programs; account for ownership, lifetime and error paths.

phases.title: Algorithms
phases.topics: data structures; complexity and Big O; searching; sorting; trees; graphs; dynamic programming; correctness; benchmarking
phases.outcome: Justify correctness and complexity; compare measured behavior with predictions.

phases.title: Computer Systems
phases.topics: compilation; machine code; linking; loading; memory layout; stack; heap; caches; system calls; processes; threads; concurrency; reverse engineering
phases.outcome: Trace compiled execution and allocations; distinguish model, source evidence and observation.

phases.title: Operating Systems
phases.topics: architecture; scheduling; virtual memory; filesystems; interrupts; system calls; synchronization; kernel/user boundary
phases.outcome: Explain and test a small kernel change in an isolated emulator.

phases.title: Networking
phases.topics: fundamentals; TCP/IP; addressing; routing; TCP; UDP; DNS; HTTP; TLS; sockets; network programming; distributed communication
phases.outcome: Trace a request across interfaces and explain partial I/O and disconnections.

phases.title: Databases and Data Systems
phases.topics: data models; relational modeling; SQL; indexes; transactions; concurrency; query execution; storage engines; B-trees; warehouses; lakes; pipelines; lineage; metadata; quality
phases.outcome: Build persistence and recovery with explicit transactional boundaries.

phases.title: Information Science and Scientific Reasoning
phases.topics: data, information and knowledge; fact and claim; evidence; context; metadata; provenance; measurement; uncertainty; source criticism; scientific method; experimental design; sampling; correlation and causation; reproducibility and replication
phases.outcome: Trace a claim back to collection and measurement; delimit what the evidence supports.

phases.title: Data Science
phases.topics: probability; statistics; inference; regression; Bayesian reasoning; acquisition; cleaning; validation; EDA; visualization; feature engineering; experimental analysis; scientific computing
phases.outcome: Produce a reproducible analysis with uncertainty, leakage checks and data provenance.

phases.title: Data Security and Cybersecurity
phases.topics: principles; threat modeling; authentication; authorization; access control; cryptography; encryption; hashing; MACs; signatures; integrity; authenticity; secure storage and transmission; network, application and database security; vulnerability analysis; monitoring; incident response; forensics
phases.outcome: Test security boundaries of a local pipeline against an explicit threat model.

phases.title: Privacy and Trusted Information
phases.topics: classification; minimization; anonymization; pseudonymization; differential privacy; privacy-preserving analytics; auditability; traceability; integrity verification; secure sharing; retention; secure deletion
phases.outcome: Verify recorded transformations while stating what provenance cannot establish about reality.

phases.title: Programming Languages and Compilers
phases.topics: language design; lexing; parsing; AST; semantic analysis; types; interpreters; bytecode; virtual machines; code generation; runtimes; garbage collection
phases.outcome: Implement a language with defined evaluation and error semantics.

phases.title: Distributed Systems
phases.topics: distributed computation; replication; consistency; consensus; fault tolerance; distributed transactions; scalability; distributed storage
phases.outcome: State a fault model, inject failures and compare observed histories with promised semantics.

phases.title: Machine Learning and AI
phases.topics: regression; classification; clustering; evaluation; optimization; neural networks; deep learning; representation learning; ML systems; model security and reliability
phases.outcome: Derive and check gradients; evaluate generalization separately from training performance.

phases.title: Embedded Systems and Robotics
phases.topics: electronics; microcontrollers; embedded C; sensors; actuators; firmware; real-time systems; control; robotics; autonomous systems; hardware/software integration
phases.outcome: Measure sensor behavior and timing; explain calibration, control and physical limitations.

phases.title: Computational Biology
phases.topics: biology; chemistry; genetics; molecular biology; biochemistry; evolution; bioinformatics; genomics; systems biology; mathematical biology; synthetic biology
phases.outcome: Analyze public biological data while separating computational output from biological interpretation.

phases.title: Experimental Research
phases.topics: research questions; literature; evidence evaluation; measurement; design; collection; analysis; reproduction; replication; reproducibility; documentation; scientific writing
phases.outcome: Reproduce a bounded published result; document discrepancies and limits before proposing extensions.

units.title: Source-grounded observation and study protocol
units.exit_gate: Identify the supplied edition and a source locator; distinguish a quotation, explanation, prediction and observation. Local intake is inspected; learner demonstration remains pending.

units.title: Representation and computation foundations
units.exit_gate: Choose an explicit encoding, decode examples and explain assumptions; first book unit chosen only after actual source mapping.

units.title: Logic, gates and combinational arithmetic
units.exit_gate: Derive truth tables and demonstrate exhaustive small-input tests, including overflow boundaries.

units.title: State, memory, CPU and machine instructions
units.exit_gate: Predict register, memory and program-counter changes through a short instruction trace.

units.title: Programming, debugging, files and Git
units.exit_gate: Write tested small programs; trace pointers and object lifetimes; preserve work with local Git.

units.title: Minimal process and file-descriptor bridge
units.exit_gate: Explain process creation, execution, waiting and descriptor redirection before implementing the shell.

units.title: Proof, discrete structures and growth
units.exit_gate: Use sets, functions, induction, invariants, sums and logarithms to justify a simple bound.

units.title: Data structures and algorithms
units.exit_gate: Explain correctness, test edge cases, and measure representative workloads without conflating timing with complexity.

units.title: Compiled programs and systems mechanisms
units.exit_gate: Trace linking, memory layout, syscalls and concurrency; allocator and compiled-program inspection share one systems lab.

units.title: Operating-system internals
units.exit_gate: Trace a kernel operation and test an isolated xv6 modification.

units.title: Networks and network programs
units.exit_gate: Implement local TCP and HTTP servers with framing, partial I/O and disconnect tests; TLS use precedes crypto internals.

units.title: Storage, databases and pipelines
units.exit_gate: Test indexing, transactions and recovery; distributed database sections wait for U17; Rust bridge needed before toydb code.

units.title: Evidence, measurement and scientific reasoning
units.exit_gate: Trace claim → analysis → data → measurement → collection → source → reality; identify confounding and uncertainty.

units.title: Probability, statistics and data analysis
units.exit_gate: Model sampling and uncertainty; acquire linear algebra before multivariate regression and calculus before continuous models.

units.title: Controlled security and cryptography
units.exit_gate: Apply modular arithmetic and discrete probability before crypto; test local threat boundaries with synthetic data.

units.title: Privacy and verifiable provenance
units.exit_gate: Specify a privacy threat model and distinguish integrity/authenticity from evidential truth; prove a small privacy claim before advanced analytics.

units.title: Languages and compilers
units.exit_gate: Implement syntax and semantics with negative tests; inspect Java prerequisites if following the original Java implementation.

units.title: Distributed storage and computation
units.exit_gate: Choose an original consensus paper before consensus implementation; record safety/liveness assumptions and fault traces.

units.title: ML, gradients and evaluation
units.exit_gate: First pass matrix algebra, derivatives, partial derivatives and chain-rule diagnostics; compare analytical and numerical gradients.

units.title: Physical measurement, electronics and control
units.exit_gate: Verify circuit/physics sources; pass units, circuits, mechanics, calculus and differential-equation bridge before control; simulate before selecting hardware.

units.title: Biological foundations and computation
units.exit_gate: Verify chemistry and biology sources; establish chemistry, cell biology, genetics and evolution before interpreting sequence analyses; no wet-lab work planned.

units.title: Bounded research reproduction
units.exit_gate: Select one original paper and domain prerequisites; reproduce an analysis and delimit agreement, disagreement and uncertainty.

units.title: Counting, quantities and units
units.exit_gate: Use quantities/units and ratios correctly in an internal systems problem.

units.title: Finite positional representations
units.exit_gate: Derive word range, byte order, modular arithmetic and signed interpretation.

units.title: State, logic and invariants
units.exit_gate: Trace a transition table and justify initialization/preservation.

units.title: Electrical quantities and digital abstraction
units.exit_gate: Derive energy/power relations and separate logical tests from device measurements.

units.title: C interface reading bridge
units.exit_gate: Explain function, object, pointer, extent and output ownership in the bounded example.
